definitions.definition: An EC 3.4.24.* (metalloendopeptidase) inhibitor that interferes with the action of neprilysin (EC 3.4.24.11).
An organic heteropentacyclic compound that is naloxone in which the keto group is replaced by a PEG moiety. Used for treatment of opioid-induced constipation.
A polyester polymer composed of repeating composed of repeating (R)-3-hydroxybutanoyl units.
A N-acylglycinate that is the conjugate base of glycodeoxycholic acid.
A dicarboxylic acid monoanion that is the conjugate base of 2-(2-carboxyethyl)-4-methyl-5-propylfuran-3-carboxylic acid.
A polyketide obtained by hydrolysis of the pyranone ring of monacolin L.
A glucosylceramide consisting of a β-D-glucosyl residue attached to the primary hydroxyl group of N-acylated C20 sphingosine.
A glycodiosylceramide consisting of a β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-β-D-glucosyl moiety attached to the primary hydroxyl group of N-acylated C20 sphingosine.

An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of 7-methyloctyl hydrogen sulfate. It has been isolated from Daphnia pulex and has been shown to cause morphological changes in the green alga Scenedesmus gutwinskii.

An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of (3Z)-9-methyldec-3-en-1-yl hydrogen sulfate. It has been isolated from Daphnia pulex and has been shown to cause morphological changes in the green alga Scenedesmus gutwinskii.

An organic sulfamate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of (3Z)-dec-3-en-1-ylsulfamic acid. It has been isolated from Daphnia pulex and has been shown to cause morphological changes in the green alga Scenedesmus gutwinskii.

An organic sulfamate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-ylsulfamic acid. It has been isolated from Daphnia pulex and has been shown to cause morphological changes in the green alga Scenedesmus gutwinskii.

An organic sulfamate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of nonylsulfamic acid. It has been isolated from Daphnia pulex and has been shown to cause morphological changes in the green alga Scenedesmus gutwinskii.
The (S)-enantiomer of 2,6-dimethylheptan-1-ol.

An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of (4R)-4,8-dimethylnonyl hydrogen sulfate. It has been isolated from Daphnia pulex and has been found to induce morphological changes in the phytoplankton, Scenedesmus gutwinskii.

An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-yl hydrogen sulfate. Isolated from Daphnia pulex, it induces morphological changes of phytoplankton Scenedesmus gutwinskii .

An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of (3Z,6Z,9Z)-dodeca-3,6,9-trien-1-yl hydrogen sulfate. Isolated from Daphnia pulex, it induces morphological changes of phytoplankton Scenedesmus gutwinskii .
A cholestanoid that is cholest-4-en-26-oic acid substituted by an α-hydroxy group at position 7 and an oxo group at position 3. It is an intermediate metabolite in the bile acid synthesis.
A Daphnia metabolite produced by the species Daphnia galeata.
An animal metabolite produced by arthropods such as crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimps and krill.
A steroid sulfate that is the 3-sulfate of epiandrosterone.
A 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-1D-myo-inositol in which the 1-acyl group is specified as stearoyl.
An aromatic amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 3-methylthiophene-2-carboxylic acid with the amino group of 2-amino-1-(4-isopropoxy-2-methylphenyl)-2-methylpropan-1-one.
An octadecadienoate that is the conjugate base of dihomolinoleic acid.
A chrysopine formally derived from β-<small>D</small>-fructopyranose.
A sulfuric ester obtained by the formal condensation of (3Z)-dodec-3-en-1-ol with sulfuric acid.
A member of the class of sulfamic acids that is sulfamic acid in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by a (3Z)-dec-3-en-1-yl group.
A member of the class of sulfamic acids that is sulfamic acid in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by a (9-methyldecyl) group.
A lipoyl-AMP(1−) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH group of (R)-lipoyl-AMP; major species at pH 7.3.
A lipoamide obtained by condensation of the carboxy group of (R)-lipoic acid with ammonia.
The (R)-enantiomer of S6-acetyldihydrolipoamide.
A member of the class of sulfamic acids that is sulfamic acid in which one of the amino hydrogens has been replaced by a (7-methyloctyl) group.
An N6-dihydrolipoyl-L-lysine residue in which the dihydrolipoyl group has R-configuration.
An N-[9-(dichloromethylene)-1,2,3,4-tetrahydro-1,4-methanonaphthalen-5-yl]-3-(difluoromethyl)-1-methylpyrazole-4-carboxamide that is the (1S,4R)-enantiomer of benzovindiflupyr.

An aromatic amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 3-(difluoromethyl)-1-methylpyrazole-4-carboxylic acid with the amino group of 3',4'-dichloro-5-fluorobiphenyl-2-amine. A fungicide for use in cereals for key stem and leaf disease control including strobilurin-resistant septoria.
An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of 2,6-dimethylheptyl hydrogen sulfate.
The (R)-enantiomer of 2,6-dimethylheptyl hydrogen sulfate.
An alkyl sulfate that is the sulfuric ester of (4R)-4,8-dimethylnonan-1-ol.
A sulfuric ester of (3Z,6Z)-dodeca-3,6-dien-1-ol.
An aromatic amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 5-chloro-1,3-dimethylpyrazole-4-carboxylic acid with the amino group of 1,1,3-trimethyl-1,3-dihydro-2-benzofuran-4-amine.
An α-amino-acid residue anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group of N6-[(R)-S8-succinyldihydrolipoyl]-L-lysine residue; major species at pH 7.3.

A member of the class of 2,5-diketopiperazines that is 2,5-diketopiperazine which is substituted at positions 3 and 6 by 3-(hydroxyamino)propyl groups in which the nitrogens have been acylated by (2E)-5-hydroxy-3-methylpent-2-enoyl groups. The substituent at position 3 has been further modified by having its terminal hydroxy group esterified by condensation with the carboxy group of N2-acetyl-N5-hydroxy-L-ornithine in which the N5 nitrogen has been acylated by a (2E)-5-hydroxy-3-methylpent-2-enoyl group.

A racemate comprising equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-penflufen. A fungicide used in furrow and seed piece treatment use on potatoes and as a seed treatment for legume vegetables, cereal grains, oil seeds and alfalfa.
5-fluoro-1,3-dimethyl-N-[2-(4-methylpentan-2-yl)phenyl]pyrazole-4-carboxamide that is the (R)-enantiomer of penflufen.
An aromatic amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 1-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)pyrazole-4-carboxylic acid with the amino group of 2-(4-methylpentan-2-yl)thiophen-3-amine.
A 1-methyl-N-[2-(4-methylpentan-2-yl)-3-thienyl]-3-(trifluoromethyl)pyrazole-4-carboxamide that is the (R)-enantiomer of penthiopyrad.
A family of macrolide antifungal compounds isolated from Streptomyces bacteria.
An acyl-CoA resulting from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (3R)-3-amino-3-phenylpropanoic acid.

A diastereoisomeric mixture consisting of the two possible cis-isomers as well as the two possible trans-isomers of sedaxane. Used in seed treatment for the control of pathogens such as Ascomycetes and Oomycetes species in crops such as fruit and wheat.
A glucosylceramide consisting of a β-D-glucosyl residue attached to the primary hydroxyl group of N-acyl-(4E,6E)-tetradecasphingadienine.
A glucosylceramide consisting of a β-D-glucosyl residue attached to the primary hydroxyl group of N-acyl-(4E,6E)-hexadecasphingadienine.

An enoate ester that is the methyl ester of (2E)-2-(2-{[2-chloro-4-(trifluoromethyl)phenoxy]methyl}phenyl)-3-methoxyprop-2-enoic acid. A fungicide active against various fungal infections including downy mildew, blight, powdery mildew and rice blast.
A hydroxamic acid anion resulting from the removal of a proton from each of the hydroxamic acid groups of desferrialbomycin δ<small><sub>1</sub></small>.
A 2-{2-[(2,5-dimethylphenoxy)methyl]phenyl}-2-methoxy-N-methylacetamide that is the (S)-enantiomer of mandestrobin.
An iron(III) hydroxamate in which desferrialbomycin δ<small><sub>2</sub></small>(3−) is complexed to iron(III).
A hydroxamic acid anion resulting from the removal of a proton from each of the hydroxamic acid groups of desferrialbomycin ε.

A monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of (2E)-{2-[(2,5-dimethylphenoxy)methyl]phenyl}(methoxyimino)acetic acid with the amino group of methylamine. A fungicide used for disease control in cereals, vegetables and turf.
A sphingolipid comprising an unspecified fatty acyl group attached to the nitrogen of L-erythro-sphingosine.
A galactosylceramide in which a β-D-galactosyl residue is attached to the primary hydroxy group of 2-N-(2-hydroxyacyl)sphinganine.

An oxime O-ether that is the O-methyl oxime of (2-{[6-(2-chlorophenoxy)-5-fluoropyrimidin-4-yl]oxy}phenyl)(5,6-dihydro-1,4,2-dioxazin-3-yl)methanone. A fungicide used for disease control of potatoes and a wide range of vegetables.
A cationic sphingoid obtained by the protonation of the amino group of 14-methylhexadecasphingosine; major species at pH 7.3.
The (1S,3R,5S)-stereoisomer of pinocarveol.

An N-acylpiperidine that is N-acetyl 4-(1,3-thiazol-2-yl)piperidine in which the thiazole ring is substituted at position 4 by a 5-(2,6-difluorophenyl)-4,5-dihydro-1,2-oxazol-3-yl group and in which one of the hydrogens of the acetyl group is replaced by a 5-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)-1H-pyrazol-1-yl group.
A polyunsaturated fatty acid anion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group of (2E,6E)-farnesoic acid; major species at pH 7.3.

A non-proteinogenic dipeptide formed from <small>L</small>-γ-glutamic acid and hercynyl-<small>L</small>-cysteine sulfoxide residues. It is an intermediate in the synthesis of ergothioneine, a compound found in certain fungi and mycobacteria.
A 1-[3-(4-tert-butylphenyl)-2-methylpropyl]piperidine that has S configuration.
An antagonist that binds to and deactivates orexin receptors.

A member of the class of morpholines that is 2,6-dimethylmorpholine in which the hydrogen attached to the nitrogen is replaced by a dodecyl group. The configuration at positions 2 and 6 is unknown or unspecified.
A 4-dodecyl-2,5-dimethylmorpholine in which both of the stereocentres have R configuration.
A phosphatidate(2−) obtained by deprotonation of both phosphate OH groups of dioleoylphosphatidic acid; major species at pH 7.3.

A hydrochloride obtained by combining olodaterol with one equivalent of hydrochloric acid. Used for long-term treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema.
A pyridinium ion obtained by protonation of the pyridine nitrogen in vorapaxar.

An EC 1.14.13.* (oxidoreductase acting on paired donors, incorporating 1 atom of oxygen, with NADH or NADPH as one donor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of methylsterol monooxygenase (EC 1.14.13.72).

definitions.definition: An EC 1.3.1.* (oxidoreductase acting on donor CH-CH group, NAD<small><sup>+</small></sup> or NADP<small><sup>+</small></sup> as acceptor) inhibitor that interferes with the action of Δ<small><sup>14</small></sup>-sterol reductase (EC 1.3.1.70).

definitions.definition: An organic cation obtained by protonation of the two tertiary amino groups of eprazinone.
A member of the class of pyrazoles in which one of the carbons of the pyrazole ring is substituted by an oxo group.
A 5-[1-hydroxy-2-(isopropanylamino)ethyl]benzene-1,3-diol that is the (R)-enantiomer of orciprenaline.

A member of the class of benzotriazines that is 1,2,4-benzotriazine 1-oxide which is substituted by chlorine at position 7 and by a 1H-imidazol-1-yl group at position 3. A fungicide, it is used as a seed treatment for control of seed-borne Pyrenophora graminea and Pyrenophora teres in barley.
A fatty acid methyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 12-HPETE with methanol.
A cyclic tetrapyrrole anion arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group and the C-21 posiiton of chlorophyllide a. It is the major microspecies at pH 7.3 (according to Marvin v 6.2.0.).

A cyclic tetrapyrrole anion that is the conjugate base of protochlorophyllide, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group and formation of a carbide ion. It is the major microspecies at pH 7.3 (according to Marvin v 6.2.0.).
A 2-sec-butyl-4,6-dinitrophenyl 3-methylbut-2-enoate that is the (S)-enantiomer of binapacryl.
An organohosphate oxoanion resulting from the removal of all three protons from the diphosphate group of all-cis-polyprenyl diphosphate(3−). Major structure at pH 7.3.

A mixture of 2,4-dinitro-6-octylphenyl crotonates in which 'octyl' is a mixture of 1-methylheptyl, 1-ethylhexyl and 1-propylpentyl groups. A component of dinocap, which is used as a protectant fungicide for powdery mildew control. The most active component is where R = 1-methylheptyl, which has the ISO common name meptyldinocap.
A member of the class of furans carrying two formyl substituents at positions 2 and 5.
A furancarboxylate that is the conjugate base of 5-formyl-2-furoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

A monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group from 4,5-dimethyl-2-(trimethylsilyl)thiophene-3-carboxlic acid with the amino group of allylamine. A fungicide seed dressing for cereals used mainly to control 'take-all'.
A primary ammonium ion obtained by protonation of the amino group of any N5-acyl-L-ornithine ester; major species at pH 7.3.
An α-amino-acid residue anion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of O-phospho-L-serine residue; major speices at pH 7.3.

An enamide resulting from the formal condensation of (2Z)-3-(4-chlorophenyl)-3-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)acrylic acid with the amino group of morpholine. The agricultural fungicide dimethomorph is a mixture of (E)- and (Z)-dimethomorph; only the Z isomer has fungicidal activity.
An enamide resulting from the formal condensation of (2E)-3-(4-fluorophenyl)-3-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)acrylic acid with the amino group of morpholine.
A carbohydrate acid anion that is the conjugate base of 3,6-anhydro-<small>L</small>-galactonic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
An O-(S-3-oxoacylpantetheine-4'-phosphoryl)serine(1−) residue in which the S-acyl group is specified as 3-oxododecanoyl.
A guanidinium ion obtained by protonation of iminoarginine; major species at pH 7.3.
An oxo monocarboxylic acid that is oxoacetic acid substituted by a (2,6-diethylphenyl)(methoxymethyl)amino group at position 2. It is a metabolite of the herbicide alachlor.
A methyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of thifensulfuron with methanol. It is used  as a post-emergence herbicide for the control of grass and broad-leaved weeds.
A sulfonamide that is benzenesulfonamide substituted by an acetylamino group at position 4 and a 1,3-thiazol-2-yl group at the nitrogen atom. It is a metabolite of sulfathiazole.
A member of the class of sulfamides that is N,N-dimethylsulfuric diamide substituted by a 4-methylphenyl group at the amino nitrogen atom. It is a metabolite of the agrochemical tolylfluanid.
A diamino-1,3,5-triazine that is 1,3,5-triazin-2-ol substituted by a tert-butylamino group at position 4 and an ethylamino group at position 6. It is a metabolite of the herbicide terbutylazine,
A monocarboxylic acid that is oxoacetic acid substituted by a (4-fluorophenyl)(propan-2-yl)amino group at position 2. It is a metabolite of the herbicide flufenacet.
An organosulfonic acid that is 2-oxoethanesulfonic acid substituted by a phenyl(propan-2-yl)amino group at position 2. It is a metabolite of the herbicide propachlor.
A heteroaryl hydroxy compound that is pyridazin-3-ol substituted by an amino group at position 5 and a chloro group at position 4. It is a metabolite of the herbicide chloridazone.

A pyridazinone that is pyridazin-3(2H)-one substituted by an amino group at position 5, a chloro group at position 4 and a methyl group at position 2. It is a metabolite of the herbicide chloridazone.jfuyklriltoil
A fluorotelomer that is dec-2-enoic acid substituted by fluoro groups at positions 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9, 10, 10 and 10 respectively.
A sulfoxide derivative of the drug ranitidine.
A N-oxide derivative of ranitidine.
A racemate composed of equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-climbazole. It is a topically applied antifungal agent used to treat human fungal skin infections.
A pyrimidine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside 5'-diphosphate that is 2'-deoxycytidine 5'-diphosphate (CDP) substituted by a hydroxymethyl group at position 5.
A member of the class of benzamides that is N,N-dimethylbenzamide substituted by a formylamino group at position 4 and a [(4,6-dimethoxypyrimidin-2-yl)carbamoyl]sulfamoyl group at position 2.
A dipeptide composed of N-(3,3-dimethylbutyl)-L-aspartic acid and methyl L-phenylalanate units joined by a peptide linkage.
A sulfonamide that is the N-ethyl derivative of perfluorooctane sulfonamidoacetic acid.
A member of the class of phenylureas that is urea substituted by a p-cumenyl group at position 1. It is a metabolite of the herbicide isoproturon.
An  organoiodine compound that is 2,4,6-triiodobenzoic acid substituted by an acetylamino group at position 3 and a (2-hydroxyethyl)carbamoyl group at position 5. It is used as a contrast medium.
A 1,2-thiazole that is 1,2-thiazol-3(2H)-one substituted by chloro groups at positions 4 and 5 and an octyl group at position 2. It is used as a fungicide.

A pyrazolooxadiazepine that is 7-oxo-1,2,4,5-tetrahydro-7H-pyrazolo[1,2-d][1,4,5]oxadiazepin which is substituted at positions 8 and 9 by 2,6-diethyl-4-methylphenyl and pivaloyloxy groups, respectively. A pro-herbicide (by hydrolysis of the pivalate ester to give the corresponding enol), it is used for control of grass weeds in cereal crops.

A pyrazolone that is 1,2-dihydro-3H-pyrazol-3-one substituted by a formaylamino group at position 4, methyl groups at positions 1 and 5 and a phenyl group at position 2. It is a metabolite of aminophenazone.

A nitrile that is pentanenitrile substituted by a 3,4-dimethoxyphenyl group at position 2, a methylamino group at position 4 and an isopropyl group at position 2. It is a metabolite of the drug verapamil.
A dibenzoazepine that is 10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[b,f]azepine-5-carboxamide substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 10 and 11. It is a metabolite of the drug carbamazepine.

An  organic phosphate that is diethyl hydrogen phosphate in which the hydrogen of the hydroxy group has been replaced by a 6-methyl-2-(propan-2-yl)pyrimidin-4-yl group. It is a metabolite of the pesticide diazinon.
A member of the  dihydrochalcones that is 3,2',4',6'-tetrahydroxy-4-methoxydihydrochalcone attached to a neohesperidosyl residue at position 4' via glycosidic linkage. It is found in sweet orange.
A N-arylpiperazine that is piperazine substituted by a 3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group at position 1. A serotonergic agonist used as a recreational drug.
A dialkyl phosphate in which the alkyl group specified is perfluorooctyl.
A monochloropyridine that is 2-chloropyridine substituted by a [2-(carbamoylimino)-1,3-thiazolidin-3-yl]methyl group at position 5. It is a metabolite of the insecticide thiacloprid.
The ethyl ester of 3-(3,5-dichlorophenyl)-5-methyl-2,4-dioxo-1,3-oxazolidine-5-carboxylic acid.
An ethyl 3-(3,5-dichlorophenyl)-5-methyl-2,4-dioxo-1,3-oxazolidine-5-carboxylate that is the (S)-enantiomer of chlozolinate.
An anionic amino-acid residue formed by loss of both protons from the phospho group of Nτ-phospho-L-histidine residue, the principal form present at pH 7.3.

The stereoisomer of isopropyl (3-methyl-1-{[1-(4-methylphenyl)ethyl]amino}-1-oxobutan-2-yl)carbamate resulting from the formal condensation of L-valine Nα-isopropyl carbamate with (1R)-1-(p-tolyl)ethylamine.
A 2-(4-{[5-(trifluoromethyl)pyridin-2-yl]oxy}phenoxy)propanoic acid that has R configuration. It is the active enantiomer of the herbicide fluazifop and is the major metabolite of fluazifop-P-butyl.
A pyrimidine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside 5'-triphosphate that is 2'deoxycytidine-5'-triphosphate substituted by a hydroxymethyl group at position 5.

A carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of L-valine with (1R)-1-(6-fluoro-1,3-benzothiazol-2-yl)ethylamine and replacement of one of the hydrogens attached to the α-amino group by a carboxy group. It is the active form of the fungicide benthiavalicarb isopropyl (in which the carbamic acid group has been converted to the corresponding isopropyl ester).
A 1-[2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-2-{[4-(phenylsulfanyl)benzyl]oxy}ethyl]imidazole that is the (R)-enantiomer of fenticonazole.
An organic nitrate salt obtained by reaction of equimolar amounts of (R)-fenticonazole and nitric acid.

An organic sodium salt that is the sodium salt of pravastatin. A reversible inhibitor of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA), it is used for lowering cholesterol and preventing cardiovascular disease. It is one of the lower potency statins, but has the advantage of fewer side effects compared with lovastatin and simvastatin.
An organic cation obtained by protonation of the imidazole group of (R)-fenticonazole.
A monocarboxylic acid amide resulting from the condensation of the carboxy group of p-chloromandelic acid propargyl ether with the amino group of 2-[3-methoxy-4-(prop-2-yn-1-yloxy)phenyl]ethylamine.
An organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH group of any fatty acyl-AMP; major species at pH 7.3.
A fatty acyl-AMP(1−) obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH group of dodecanoyl-AMP; the major species at pH 7.3.
An α-amino-acid residue derived from O-adenyl-L-tyrosine.

An essential oil consisting of approximately one hundred hydrocarbon and terpenoid components obtained by steam distillation from the leaves and terminal branchlets of the tea tree, Melaleuca alternifolia; the yield of oil is typically 1-2% of wet plant material weight. The main components are 4-terpineol (40%), γ-terpinene (23%), α-terpinene (10%), 1,8-cineole (5%), terpinolene (3%), and p-cymene (3%).
The (R)-enantiomer of 2-(butan-2-yl)-4,6-dinitrophenol.
An organic salt in which the cation has the structure (RN)<small><sub>2</sub></small>C=N<small><sup>+</small></sup>R<small><sub>2</sub></small>.
The (S)-enantiomer of 2-(butan-2-yl)-4,6-dinitrophenol.
A member of the class of 1,3-thiazoles that is 2-[2-(pentan-3-ylidene)hydrazino]-1,3-thiazole carrying an additional 4-chlorophenyl substituent at position 4.
An  organochlorine compound that is 2-chloroacetamide substituted by a 2,4-dimethylthiophen-3-yl and a 1-methoxypropan-2-yl group at the nitrogen atom.
The (R)-enantiomer of 2-chloro-N-(2-ethyl-6-methylphenyl)-N-(1-methoxypropan-2-yl)acetamide.
The (S)-enantiomer of 2-chloro-N-(2-ethyl-6-methylphenyl)-N-(1-methoxypropan-2-yl)acetamide.
A member of the class of 1,3-thiazoles that is 2-[2-(butan-2-ylidene)hydrazino]-1,3-thiazole carrying an additional 4-chlorophenyl substituent at position 4.
The (R)-enantiomer of [(2-ethyl-6-methylphenyl)(1-methoxypropan-2-yl)amino](oxo)acetic acid.

A monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 5-(2,4-dihydroxy-5-isopropylphenyl)-4-[4-(morpholin-4-ylmethyl)phenyl]-1,2-oxazole-3-carboxylic acid with the amino group of ethylamine.

A monocarboxylic acid amide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 3,4-dichloro-1,2-thiazole-5-carboxylic acid with o-cyanoaniline. It is a fungicide used for the control of rice blast.
A 1-{2-[(2,6-dichlorobenzyl)oxy]-2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)ethyl}imidazole that is the (S)-enantiomer of isoconazole.
An organic cation obtained by protonation of the imidazole group of (R)-isoconazole.
A long-chain fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 10-PAHSA, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A long-chain fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 12-PAHSA, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
The (S)-enantiomer of 2-[(2-ethyl-6-methylphenyl)(1-methoxypropan-2-yl)amino]-2-oxoethanesulfonic acid.
A member of the class of imidazoles that carries a 2-[(7-chloro-1-benzothiophen-3-yl)methoxy]-2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)ethyl group at position 1.

A racemate comprising equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-sertaconazole nitrate. A broad spectrum antifungal with added antipruritic and anti-inflammatory activity used for treatment of various skin infections.

An organic nitrate salt obtained by reaction of equimolar amounts of arasertaconazole and nitric acid. The active R-enantiomer of sertaconazole nitrate that is used for treatment of vulvovaginal candidiasis. The racemate itself is also used as a broad-spectrum antifungal drug.
A (2-chlorophenyl)(4-fluorophenyl)pyrimidin-5-ylmethanol that has R configuration.
A long-chain fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 7-PAHSA, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A long-chain fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 8-PAHSA, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A glycophytoceramide having an α-<small>D</small>-Gal-(1→2)α-<small>D</small>Gal glycosyl group at the O-1 position and a hexacosanoyl group attached to the nitrogen.
A sphingoid that is the C<small><sub>14</sub></small>-analogue of phytosphingosine.
A member of the class of triazoles that is 1-hexyl-1H-1,2,4-triazole in which the hydrogens at position 2 of the hexyl chain are replaced by hydroxy and 2,4-dichlorophenyl groups.
A 2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-1-(1H-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)hexan-2-ol that has R configuration.
A 2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-1-(1H-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)hexan-2-ol that has S configuration.
A ketone that is butan-2-one substituted by a 4-chlorophenoxy and a 1H-imidazol-1-yl group at position 1 and 2 methyl groups at position 3.
Any alkylmercury compound in which a primary alkyl group is attached to a positively charged mercury atom.
A sterol biosynthesis inhibitor that acts by inhibiting the C14 demethylation step within fungal steroid biosynthesis.

An oxo monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 5-hydroxy-3-[(3aS,4S,5R,7aS)-7a-methyl-1,5-dioxo-octahydro-1H-inden-4-yl]propanoate, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
An organic anionic group that is ferroheme c(2−) bound to cytochrome c by two L-cysteine residues; major species at pH 7.3.
The (R)-enantiomer of 5-(methoxymethyl)-2-[4-methyl-5-oxo-4-(propan-2-yl)-4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazol-2-yl]pyridine-3-carboxylic acid.
A ceramide phosphoethanolamine in which the sphingoid component is specified as tetradecasphingosine.

A member of the class of N-acylpiperazines obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2-fluoro-5-[(4-oxo-3,4-dihydrophthalazin-1-yl)methyl]benzoic acid with the free amino group of N-(cyclpropylcarbonyl)piperazine; used to treat advanced ovarian cancer.
The (R)-enantiomer of 2-ethoxy-3,3-dimethyl-2,3-dihydro-1-benzofuran-5-yl methanesulfonate.
A monocarboxylic acid amide that is propanamide substituted by two ethyl groups at the nitrogen atom and a naphthalen-1-yloxy group at position 2.
A glucocorticoid that is prednisone in which the oxo group at position 11 has been reduced to the corresponding β-hydroxy group. It is a drug metabolite of prednisone.
An icosanoid that is (5Z,9E,14Z)-icosa-5,9,14-trienoic acid carrying four hydroxy substituents at positions 8, 11, 12 and 20. An intermediary metabolite from the 12(R)-lipoxygenase pathway.
An acyl-CoA oxoanion resulting from the removal of all four protons from the phosphate groups of (25S)-3β-hydroxy-5-cholesten-26-oyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol 3-phosphate in which the 1- and 2-acyl substituent are specified as palmitoyl and (4Z,7Z,10Z,13Z,16Z,19Z)-docosahexaenoyl respectively.
The (S)-enantiomer of N-(butan-2-yl)-N'-ethyl-6-methoxy-1,3,5-triazine-2,4-diamine.
The (R)-enantiomer of N-(butan-2-yl)-6-chloro-N'-ethyl-1,3,5-triazine-2,4-diamine.

A member of the class of pyridopyrimidines that is 9-hydroxy-2-methyl-6,7,8,9-tetrahydropyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidin-4-one carrying an additional 2-[4-(6-fluoro-1,2-benzoxazol-3-yl)piperidin-1-yl]ethyl group at position 2.

A fatty acid ester obtained by the formal condensation of the carboxy group of hexadecanoic acid with the hydroxy group of 3-{2-[4-(6-fluoro-1,2-benzoxazol-3-yl)piperidin-1-yl]ethyl}-9-hydroxy-2-methyl-6,7,8,9-tetrahydropyrido[1,2-a]pyrimidin-4-one.
Any derivative of a proteinogenic amino acid resulting from reaction at an amino group, carboxy group, or a side-chain functional group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen by a heteroatom.
Any derivative of a non-proteinogenic amino acid resulting from reaction at an amino group or carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen by a heteroatom.

Any organonitrogen heterocyclic compound based on a morphinan skeleton. These are synthetic or semi-synthetic compounds that resemble the  morphinane (opioid) alkaloids in their pharmacological effects.
A member of the class of imidazoles in which the hydrogen at position 1 is replaced by a 2-(allyloxy)-2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)ethyl group.
A racemate comprising equimolar amounts of (R)- and (S)-oxpoconazole. Used (as its fumarate salt) to control a variety of fungal diseases including Botrytis, Sclerotinia and Monilinia spp.
A member of the class of oxazolidines that is 2-[3-(4-chlorophenyl)propyl]-2,4,4-trimethyl-1,3-oxazolidine in which the amino hydrogen is replaced by an (imidazol-1-yl)carbonyl group.
A fumarate salt prepared from (R)-oxpoconazole by reaction of one molecule of fumaric acid for every two molecules of (R)-oxpoconazole.
A pent-4-en-1-yl 2-[(2-furylmethyl)(imidazol-1-ylcarbonyl)amino]butanoate that is the (R)-enantiomer of pefurazoate.
An acylsphingosine in which the acyl moiety contains 24 carbons and 2 double bonds.
An organic heteropentacyclic compound that is the 8'-O-β-D-glucoside of dalcochinin.
A sphingomyelin in which the total number of carbons in the fatty acyl group is 24 with 2 double bonds.
A 1-(biphenyl-4-yloxy)-3,3-dimethyl-1-(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)butan-2-ol that is the (1S,2S)-diastereomer of bitertanol.
A flavonoid oxoanion that is the conjugate base of dalpatein, obtained by deprotonation of the 7-hydroxy group. It is the major microspecies at pH 7.3 (according to Marvin v 6.2.0.).
A 26-hydroxycholest-4-en-3-one in which the 25-position has S-configuration.
A methoxyisoflavan that is isoflavan substituted by a hydroxy group at position 2', methoxy groups at positions 6 and 3', a 2-carboxyethenyl group at position 5' and a sulfoxy group at position 4.
An N-acyl-D-galactosylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is composed of 24 carbons, 2 double bonds and a hydroxyl at C2.
An N-acyl-D-galactosylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is composed of 26 carbons and 1 double bond.
An N-acyl-D-galactosylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is composed of 25 carbons, 1 double bond and a hydroxy group at C2.
A sphingomyelin in which the total number of carbons in the sphingoid base and fatty acyl groups is 41 with 1 double bond.

A polysaccharide derivative comprising a trisaccharide repeating unit consisting of N-acetyl-β-D-mannosaminouronic acid, 3,N-diacetyl-α-L-fucosamine and N-acetyl-β-D-fucosamine residues linked sequentially (1→4) and (1→3), with the trisaccharide repeats themselves being linked (1→4); corresponds to the serotype 5 (CP5) capsular polysaccharide of Staphylococcus aureus.
A UDP-N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alaninate(3−) in which the D-muramoyl fragment has α-configuration at its anomeric centre; major species at pH 7.3.
An enoate ester that is the methyl ester of (2E,3Z,5E)-6-(4-chloro-3-methoxyphenyl)-2-(methoxymethylene)-3-methylhexa-3,5-dienoic acid.
An ethyl [4-({[2-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-2-(imidazol-1-ylmethyl)-1,3-dioxolan-4-yl]methyl}sulfanyl)phenyl]carbamate in which both stereocentres have S-configuration.
A hydroxy fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 14-hydroxypalmitic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A organonitrogen heterocyclic compound consisting of 2,3,1-benzodiazaborinine substituted at positions 1 and 2 by hydroxy and 4-toluenesufonyl groups respectively.
A diterpenoid obtained by hydroxylation of one of the terminal methyl groups of geranylgeraniol.
A 1-O-alkyl-sn-glycerol in which the alkyl group has a saturated bond between carbons 1 and 2.

A macrolide consisting resulting from the formal lactonisation of the carboxy group of (2E,4E,6R,7S,8S,10E,12E,14S,15R,16S,17R,18S)-18-[(2R,4R,5S,6R)-4-{[(2E)-3-carboxyprop-2-enoyl]oxy}-2-hydroxy-5,6-dimethyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-yl]-7,15,17-trihydroxy-14-methoxy-2,4,6,8,10,16-hexamethylnonadeca-2,4,10,12-tetraenoic acid with the hydroxy group at position 15. It is active against SV40 tumour cells, and inhibits the growth of solid tumour-derived cell lines such as DLD-1 human colon cancer cells with increased cells in G1 and S phases.

A member of the class of imidazoquinolines that is 3-methyl-2-oxo-2,3-dihydro-1H-imidazo[4,5-c]quinoline substituted at position 1 by a 4-(1-cyanoisopropyl)phenyl group and at position 8 by a pyrimidin-5-yl group.
Any steroid lactone that is a C23 steroid with a six-membered lactone ring at C-17 and its substituted derivatives. They form the aglycone constituents of cardiac glycosides.

A non-proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>D</small>-asparagine at the amino group, the carboxy group, or the carboxamide, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>D</small>-asparagine by a heteroatom.
The (5β)-stereoiosmer of bufadienolide.
A hydroxy-amino acid that is aspartic acid in which one of the methylene hydrogens has been replaced by a hydroxy group.

A non-proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from the formal reaction of <small>D</small>-glutamic acid at the amino group or either carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>D</small>-glutamic acid by a heteroatom.
A dithiocarbamic acid resulting from the formal addition of a molecule of carbon disulfide to each amino group of ethylenediamine.

A non-proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from the formal reaction of <small>D</small>-glutamine at the amino group, carboxy group, or carboxamide, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>D</small>-glutamine by a heteroatom.
An O-(S-acylpantetheine-4'-phosphoryl)serine(1−) residue in which the S-acyl group is specified as (9Z)-hexadecenoyl.
A member of the class of triazoles that is 1-hydroxy-3,3-dimethyl-1-(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)butan-2-one in which the hydroxyl hydrogen is replaced by a 4-chlorophenyl group.
A 1-(4-chlorophenoxy)-3,3-dimethyl-1-(1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)butan-2-one that is the (S)-enantiomer of triadimefon.
A monocarboxylic acid amide obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2-(2,4-dichlorophenoxy)propanoic acid with the amino group of 2-amino-2,3-dimethylbutanenitrile.
A monounsaturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 9,10-DiHOME, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

synonyms.name: Phosphonic acid monoethyl ester aluminum salt

definitions.definition: An aluminium salt composed of ethyl phosphonate anions and aluminium cations in a 3:1 ratio. A fungicide for various horticultural crops used to control a range of diseases including Phytophthora, Pythium and Plasmopara .
An organic sulfate that consists of dihydroresveratrol substituted by a sulfate group at position 3. It is a metabolite of dihydroresveratrol.
A monoacyl α,α-trehalose in which the acyl group is specified as palmitoyl (hexadecanoyl) and is located at position 2.
A monoatomic trication derived from gallium.
Any organic sulfate that is the monosulfate derivative of dihydroresveratrol.
Any stilbenol that is the monosulfate derivative of resveratrol.
Any  stilbenol that consists of  dihydroresveratrol attached to a sulfate and a β-<small>D</small>-glucosiduronic acid residue at unspecified positions.
Any  stilbenol that is the disulfate derivative of resveratrol.
Any stilbenol that consists of resveratrol attached to a sulfate and a β-<small>D</small>-glucosiduronic acid residue at unspecified positions.
Any phospho sugar that is the phosphate derivative of pentose.
A long-chain fatty acyl-CoA(4−) arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions of tridecanoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
A palmitate ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of palmitic acid with the hydroxy group of tetradecan-1-ol.

A lipid A derivative that consists of a branched octasaccharide phosphate made up from two D-galactose residues, two N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residues, a D-glucose residue, two L-glycero-D-manno-heptose residues (one of which is phosphoethanolamine-substituted on O-3), with linkages as shown and with a 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid (2-keto-3-deoxy-D-mannooctanoic acid, Kdo) residue at the reducing end connected via an α(2→6) linkage to a de-O-acylated lipid A. Corresponds to the de-O-acylated lipid A conjugate of the core oligosaccharide of Neisseria meningitidis.

A lipid A derivative that consists of a branched pentasaccharide phosphate made up from a D-glucose residue, an N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residue, two L-glycero-D-manno-heptose residues (one of which is phosphoethanolamine-substituted on O-3), with linkages as shown and with a 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid (2-keto-3-deoxy-D-mannooctanoic acid, Kdo) residue at the reducing end connected via an α(2→6) linkage to a de-O-acylated lipid A. Corresponds to the de-O-acylated lipid A conjugate of the galE mutant of the core oligosaccharide of Neisseria meningitidis.

A lipid A derivative that consists of a linear tetrasaccharide phosphate comprising an N-acetyl-α-D-glucosamine residue,an L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residue phosphoethanolamine-substituted on O-3, another L-glycero-α-D-manno-heptose residue and a 3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid (2-keto-3-deoxy-D-mannooctanoic acid, Kdo) in a (1→2), (1→3), (1→5) sequence, with the Kdo residue at the reducing end connected via an α(2→6) linkage to a de-O-acylated lipid A. Corresponds to the de-O-acylated lipid A conjugate of the icsB mutant of the core oligosaccharide of Neisseria meningitidis.
An  acetate ester that is phenyl acetate substituted by an acetylamino group at position 2 and a methyl group at position 4.
A hydroxyretinoic glucuronide that is all-trans-4-hydroxyretinoic acid attached to a β-D-glucuronic acid residue via a glycosidic linkage.
A C<small><sub>9</sub></small>-acylcarnitine in which the acyl group specified is 2,6-dimethylheptanoyl.
A monocarboxylic acid amide that is acetamide substituted by a methoxy group at position 2 and a 3-oxo-3-(pyrrolidin-1-yl)propyl group at the nitrogen atom.
An O-(S-2-carboxyacylpantetheine-4'-phosphoryl)-L-serine(2−) residue in which the S-acyl group is specified as 2-carboxytetradecanoyl.
A ketoretinoic glucuronide obtained by the glycosylation of the carboxy group of all-trans-4-oxoretinoic acid with β-glucuronic acid.

A proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>L</small>-isoleucine at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>L</small>-isoleucine by a heteroatom.

An N-alkylpyrrolidine that is acrivastine in which the pyridine ring is lacking the propenoic acid substituent. It is a sedating antihistamine that is used (generally as the monohydrochloride monohydrate) for the relief of the symptoms of uticaria, rhinitis, and various pruritic skin disorders.
An ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of the pyrrolidine nitrogen of tripoloidine. It is the major species at pH 7.3.
A sialodiaosylceramide that is an α-N-acetylneuraminosyl-(2→3)-β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-β-D-glucosyl-N-acylsphingosine in which the acyl group on nitrogen is (15Z)-tetracos-15-enoyl.
An O-(S-2-alkyl-3-oxoacyl-pantetheine-4'-phosphoryl)-L-serine(1−) residue in which the S-2-alkyl-3-oxoacyl-group is specified as 2-tetradecyl-3-oxooctadecanoyl.
An amino-acid cation that is the conjugate acid of 3,6-diaminohexanoic acid resulting from protonation of both amino groups and deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

A non-proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>D</small>-phenylalanine at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>D</small>-phenylalanine by a heteroatom.
A 2-pyranone in which the hydrogens at positions 4 and 6 of 2H-pyran-2-one are replaced by hydroxy and undecyl groups respectively.
A 3-sn-phosphatidyl-L-serine in which the phosphatidyl acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as octadecanoyl and (3Z,6Z,9Z,12Z,15Z,18Z)-docosahexaenoyl respectively.
A 1-octadecanoyl-2-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-1D-myo-inositol in which the 2-acyl group is specified as (5Z,8Z,11Z,14Z)-icosa-5,8,11,14-tetraenoyl (arachidonoyl).

A branched hexasaccharide comprised of five α-D-mannose residues linked as shown and also to a 3-deoxy-α-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid (3-deoxy-D-manno-oct-2-ulosonic acid; Kdo) residue at the reducing end, corresponding to the core oligosaccharide of the phytopathogenic bacterium Rhizobacterium radiobacter strain Rv3.
A glycophytoceramide having an α-<small>D</small>-galactopyranosyl residue at the O-1 position and a decanoyl group attached to the nitrogen.
A 2-pyranone in which the hydrogens at positions 4 and 6 of 2H-pyran-2-one are replaced by hydroxy and heptadecyl groups respectively.
A 2-pyranone in which the hydrogens at positions 4 and 6 of 2H-pyran-2-one are replaced by hydroxy and 2-oxohenicosyl groups respectively.
A hydroperoxy fatty acid that is (6Z,8E,12Z)-octadecatrienoic acid in which the hydroperoxy group is located at position 10.

A proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>L</small>-proline at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>L</small>-proline  by a heteroatom.

A non-proteinogenic amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of <small>D</small>-threonine  at the amino group or the carboxy group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of <small>D</small>-threonine  by a heteroatom.
A hydroxy-amino acid that is tryptophan substituted by at least one hydroxy group at unspecified position.
A 3-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA(4−) oxanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of 3-hydroxytetradecanoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
A hydroxy saturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of 12-hydroxyoctadecanoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A fatty acyl-CoA(4−) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of any ω-hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
A member of the class of furoic acids that is 2-furoic acid substituted at position 5 by a formyl group.
A member of the class of furans carrying two carboxy substituents at positions 2 and 5.
An   iodoalkane that is undecane substituted by an iodo group at position 1 and a methyl group at position 2. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism.
Any organic heterotricyclic compound constructed from fused thiophene, triazole and diazepeine rings.
A 2-pyranone in which the hydrogens at positions 4 and 6 of 2H-pyran-2-one are replaced by hydroxy and heptyl groups respectively.
An alkane that is undecane substituted by a methyl group at position 4. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism.
A 2-pyranone in which the hydrogens at positions 4, 5 and 6 of 2H-pyran-2-one are replaced by hydroxy, methyl and heptadecyl groups respectively.
An anhydrohexose obtained by formation of a ring across the 3 and 6 positions of <small>L</small>-galactonic acid
The <small>D</small>-enantiomer of prolinol. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism.
A primary aliphatic amine that is propan-1,2-diamine substituted by an isopropyl group at N1 and a methyl group at position 2. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism.
A 1-acyl-2-tetradecanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphate in which the 1-acyl group is specified as tetradecanoyl (myristoyl).
A saturated fatty aldehyde formally arising from reduction of the carboxy group of nonanoic acid. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism.
A 2-methyl fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of (2S)-2-methyl-heptadecanoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A sulfoxide in which the S atom is substituted by a phenyl and (2,3-diphenylcyclopropyl)methyl group. Metabolite observed in cancer metabolism.
An alkane that is dodecane substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 7 and 10.
A  thiazolidinecarboxamide that is 1,3-thiazolidine-2-carboxamide substituted by a methyl group at position 2.
An ether consists of a hexane chain substituted by a methoxy and a methyl group at position 3.
A N-alkylpiperazine that is piperazine substituted by a methyl and a 2-aminoethyl group at the N atoms respectively.
A member of the class of dithiocarbamate anions resulting from the deprotonation of both of the dithiocarbamic acid moieties of propylene 1,2-bis(dithiocarbamic acid). The major species at pH 7.3.

An <small>L</small>-tyrosine derivative that is <small>L</small>-DOPA in which the hydrogen at position 2 on the phenyl ring is replaced by a cysteinyl group. Found in the urine of patients with melanoma.
A peptide zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of bacilysin; major species at pH 7.3.
Any mixture comprising two or more oligomycins.
A peptide zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino terminus of dapdiamide C; major species at pH 7.3.
A 2-hydroxy fatty acid anion with a chain that is composed of 24 carbons and 1 double bond (position  unspecified).
A member of the class of guanidines that is decane having guanidino groups at the 1- and 10-positions.

A member of the class of ureas that is 1H-imidazole-1-carboxamide substituted by a propyl and a 2-(2,4,6-trichlorophenoxy)ethyl group at the amino nitrogen atom. A fungicide active against a wide range of diseases affecting field crops, fruit, turf and vegetables.
A cholesterol ester obtained by the formal condensation of cholesterol with (9Z,12Z,15Z)-octadeca-9,12,15-trienoic acid.
A member of the class of benzothiazines that is 3,4-dihydro-2H-1,4-benzothiazin-3-one bearing additional hydroxy and 2-amino-2-carboxyethyl substituents at positions 5 and 7 respectively.
A cholesterol ester obtained by the formal condensation of cholesterol with all-cis-icosa-8,11,14-trienoic acid.
An organosulfate oxoanion that is the conjugate base of 2-palmitoyl-3-stearoyl-2'-sulfo-α,α-trehalose arising from deprotonation of the sulfate OH group; major species at pH 7.3.
A member of the class of cyclohexenones that is (1R,5S,6R)-4-amino-5-hydroxy-1-(hydroxymethyl)-7-oxabicyclo[4.1.0]hept-3-en-2-one in which one of the amino hydrogens is replaced by an acetyl group.
A member of the class of cyclitols that is valiolone in which the stererocentre at position 5 has been inverted.
A polyunsaturated fatty acid anion composed of 24 carbons with 2 double bonds in unknown positions.
A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol that has myristoyl and linoleoyl as 1- and 2-acyl groups respectively.
A 2-hydroxy fatty acid anion with a chain that is composed of 24 carbons and 2 double bond (positions unspecified).
A linear dextrin or short chained amylose (DP 20-30) that can be produced by enzymatic hydrolysis of the α-1,6 glycosidic bonds or debranching amylopectin.
A cardiolipin in which all four phosphatidyl acyl groups are specified as linoleoyl.

Any of the lignans with a 9-aryl-1-oxo-1,3-dihydronaphtho[2,3-c]furan-4-yl glycoside skeleton originally isolated from Cleistanthus collinus, a toxic deciduous shrub. While all parts of the plant are poisonous, the leaves in particular are used as a suicide poison by young women in rural parts of southern India. Cleistanthins A and B have been particularly associated with the toxicity of the plant, with cleistanthin A being more potent than cleistanthin B.
A member of the class of cleistanthins that is cleistanthin A in which the 3,4-di-O-methyl-D-xylopyranosyl group is replaced by a β-D-glucopyranosyl group.
A fatty acyl-AMP that results from the formal condensation of the phosphoryl group of AMP with the carboxyl group of hexadecanoic (palmitic) acid.

A member of the class of cleistanthins that is cleistanthin C in which the hydroxy group at position 4 of the 2,3-di-O-methyl-β-D-xylopyranosyl moiety has been converted to the corresponding 2,3,5-tri-O-methyl-D-xylofuranoside.
A polyprenylhydroquinone having the structure of a ubiquinol with hydroxy replacing methoxy at C-5.
A FAHFA (fatty acid ester of a hydroxy fatty acid) obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of palmitic acid with the hydroxy group of 9-hydroxyoctadecanoic acid (9-hydroxystearic acid).
A 3-demethylubiquinol in which the polyprenyl chain contains 7 prenyl units.
A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycerol in which the acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are specified as oleoyl and 8Z,11Z,14Z-eicosatrienoyl respectively.
The hydroxybenzoate anion formed by loss of a proton from the carboxy group of 3-methoxy-4-hydroxy-5-all-trans-polyprenylbenzoic acid. The major species present at pH 7.3.
A FAHFA obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of palmitic acid with the hydroxy group of 11-hydroxystearic acid.
A lysophosphatidylcholine with defined stereochemistry where the position of the acyl group is unknown.
A 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoserine(1−) that is the conjugate base of 1-stearoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoserine; major species at pH 7.3.
A FAHFA obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of palmitic acid with the hydroxy group of 12-hydroxystearic acid.
A FAHFA obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of palmitic acid with the hydroxy group of 13-hydroxystearic acid.
A N-octadecenolsphingosine-1-phosphocholine in which the acyl group specified is 9Z-octadecenoyl.
A fatty acid anion where the last 2 carbons (ω and ω−1) form an ethyl end. Formula:C3H5O2R
A 3-sn-phosphatidyl L-serine in which the phosphatidyl acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are stearoyl and 7Z,10Z,13Z,16Z-docosatetraenoyl respectively.
A 3-sn-phosphatidyl L-serine in which the phosphatidyl acyl groups at positions 1 and 2 are stearoyl and (9Z,12Z)-octadecadienoyl respectively.
A 2-methoxy-6-(all-trans-polyprenyl)phenol in which the polyprenyl component is specified as all-trans-heptaprenyl.
A 2-methoxy-6-(all-trans-polyprenyl)phenol in which the polyprenyl component is specified as all-trans-nonaprenyl.
A 1-(alk-1-enyl)-2-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine in which the alkenyl and acyl groups are specified as (1Z)-hexadecenyl and arachidonoyl respectively.
A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine in which the acyl groups specified at position 1 and 2 are palmitoyl and (7Z,10Z,13Z,16Z)-docosatetraenoyl respectively.

A biguanide compound which has isopropyl and p-chlorophenyl substituents on the terminal N atoms. A prophylactic antimalarial drug, it works by inhibiting the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase, which is involved in the reproduction of the malaria parasites Plasmodium falciparum and P. vivax within the red blood cells.

A  ketogluconic acid that is <small>L</small>-gluconic acid in which the hydroxy group at position 2 has been oxidized to a keto group.
A tetritol that is  erythritol substituted by a methyl group at position 2.

A member of the class of phenazines carrying methyl, amino and dimethylamino substituents at positions 2, 3 and 7 respectively. The free base of neutral red, which acts as a pH indicator, changing from red to yellow between pH 6.8 and 8.0.
An unsaturated fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (10E,12Z)-hexadecadienoic acid.
An ammonium ion resulting from the protonation of the nitrogen of amorolfine.
An EC 5.3.3.* (intramolecular oxidase transposing C=C bonds) inhibitor that interferes with the action of a cholestenol Δ-isomerase (EC 5.3.3.5).

definitions.definition: An amino fatty acid anion that is the  conjugate base of 5-aminopentanoic acid.
A member of the class of cyclohexanones that is cyclohexane-1,4-dionecarrying a gem-dimethyl group at position 2 and an additional methyl substituent at position 6 (the R-enantiomer).
An α-amino-acid residue derived from cysteinyl-aspartic acid.
A member of the class of azabicycloalkanes that is 1-azabicyclo[3.2.0]heptan-7-one substituted at positions 3 and 6 by (2-aminoethyl)thio and ethyl groups respectively.
An amino cyclitol glycoside that is (1R,2S,3S,4S,5S,6R)-2-amino-1,3,4,6-tetrahydroxy-5-(methylamino)cyclohexane in which the hydroxy group at position 1 is glycosylated by a heptapyranosyl residue.
An acyl-CoA(4−) oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of 3-oxochol-4-en-24-oyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
An acyl-CoA(4−) oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of 3-oxochola-4,22-dien-24-oyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
A phosphatidylcholine 30:2 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are (9Z)-hexadecenoyl and (9Z)-tetradecenoyl respectively.
A phosphatidylcholine 40:3 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are eicosanoyl and (11Z,14Z,17Z)-eicosatrienoyl respectively.
A phosphatidylcholine O-34:3 in which the alkyl and acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are hexadecyl and (6Z,9Z,12Z)-octadecatrienoyl respectively.

Sodium fluorophosphate, commonly abbreviated MFP, is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Na<small><sub>2</sub></small>PO<small><sub>3</sub></small>F. Typical for a salt, MFP is odourless, colourless, and water-soluble. This salt is an ingredient in toothpastes.
A steroid acid resulting from stereoselective oxidation of one of the terminal methyl groups of 4β-hydroxycholesterol to the corresponding carboxylic acid.
An organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH group of 4-hydroxybenzoyl-AMP; the major species at pH 7.3.
A trihydroxyanthraquinone derived from anthracene by substitution with oxo groups at C-9 and C-10 and with hydroxy groups at C-1, C-2 and C-4.
A phosphatidylcholine O-42:2 in which the alkyl and acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are icosyl and (13Z,16Z)-docosadienoyl respectively.
A phosphatidylcholine O-44:3 in which the alkyl and acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are docosyl and (10Z,13Z,16Z)-docosatrienoyl respectively.
A phosphatidylcholine O-44:4 in which the alkyl and acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are tetracosyl and (8Z,11Z,14Z,17Z)-icosatetraenoyl respectively.
An arginine derivative that is arginine substituted by two methyl groups. A "closed" class.
A 1,2-diacyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine in which the acyl groups specified at C-1 and C-2 contain 33 carbons in total with 1 double bond.
A hydrate that is the heptahydrate form of sodium molybdate.
Any strobilurin antifungal agent that contains a methoxyiminoacetate group, RC(=NOMe)CO<small><sub>2</sub></small>Me.
Heteroorganic entities that are plant metabolites which have significant antifungal properties.
An organic cation obtained by protonation of spirit blue base.

An N-acetyl-amino acid in which the amino acid specified is L-ornithine. If R1 is the acetyl group and R2 is a hydrogen then the molecule is N5-acetylornithine. If R1 is a hydrogen and R2 is acetyl group then the molecule is N2-acetylornithine.
A phosphatidylcholine O-36:2 in which the alkyl and acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are hexadecyl and (11Z,14Z)-eicosadienoyl respectively.
A straight-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid composed of eighteen carbons and containing two double bonds, both with Z-geochemistry, at positions 9 and 12 as well as a triple bond at position 6.
A glycosyloxyisoflavone that is calycosin substituted by a β-<small>D</small>-glucopyranosyl residue at position at 7 via a glycosidic linkage.
A N-acylsphingosine in which the ceramide N-acyl group is specified as heptadecanoyl.
An N-acylsphingosine in which the acyl group contains 26 carbons and 6 double bonds at unknown positions.
A ceramide phosphoethanolamine in which the sphingoid base and acyl group contains a total of 35 carbon atoms and 1 double bond.
A ceramide phosphoethanolamine (35:2) in which the specified spingoid base and acyl group specified are (4E,6E)-tetradecasphingadienine and heneicosanoyl respectively.
A ceramide phosphoethanolamine in which the sphingoid base and acyl group contains a total of 37 carbon atoms and 2 double bonds.
An α-amino acid that is cyclohexanecarboxylic acid substituted by an amino group at position 1.
A hydroxy fatty acid that is caproic (hexanoic) acid substituted by a hydroxy group at position 2.
A methoxycinnamic acid that is trans-cinnamic acid substituted by methoxy groups at positions 3' and 4' respectively.
A  primary alcohol that is cinnamyl alcohol substituted by methoxy groups at positions 3' and 4' respectively.
A member of the class of  benzoic acids that is benzoic acid substituted by an acetoxy group at position 4.
An acetate ester that is a diester obtained by the formal condensation of the two hydroxy groups of trans-p-coumaryl alcohol with two molecules of acetic acid respectively.
A member of the class of indanes that is indan-5-ol substituted by a methoxy group at position 6.
A phenyl acetate obtained by the formal condensation of the phenolic group of acetosyringone with acetic acid.
A phenyl acetate that is the diacetate derivative of coniferol.
A lignan isolated from the seeds of Crataegus pinnatifida.
A benzoate ester obtained by the formal condensation of  coniferol with benzoic acid.
A guaiacyl lignin that is syringaresinol in which one of the phenolic hydrogens is replaced by a guaiacylglycerol group. It is found in Arabidopsis thaliana.

definitions.definition: An alkyl cinnamate obtained by the formal condensation of carboxy group of 3,4-dimethoxycinnamic acid with methanol.
An acetate ester obtained by the formal condensation of the hydroxy group of veratrone with acetic acid.
Any EC 3.4.21.* (serine endopeptidase) inhibitor that interferes with the action of endopeptidase Clp (EC 3.4.21.92).
A β-lactone carrying non-8-en-1-yl and 2-(pyridin-3-yl)ethyl substituents at positions 3 and 4 respectively.
A diacylglycerol 34:0 in which the acyl groups specified at positions 1 and 2 are hexadecanoyl and octadecanoyl respectively.
A diglyceride in which the two acyl groups contain a total of 34 carbons and 5 double bonds.
The 2R stereoisomer of 2,6-dimethylheptanoyl-CoA(4−).
A diglyceride in which the two acyl groups contain a total of 36 carbons and 0 double bonds.
An organic cation resulting from the protonation of the amino group of (R)-fluoxetine.
An organic cation resulting from the protonation of the amino group of (S)-fluoxetine.
Any glycerolipid in which the acyl group at position 2 of the glycerol moiety is specified as (3E)-hexadec-3-enoyl.
An amino disaccharide comprising an N-acetyl-β-muramyl residue linked (1→4) to N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine.
A linear amino tetrasaccharide comprised of N-acetyl-α-neuraminyl, β-D-galactosyl, N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl and N-acetyl-α-D-galactosamine residues linked sequentially (2→3), (1→3) and (1→6).
A hydrate that is the dihydrate form of vanadyl sulfate.
Any anilide fungicide whose structure contains a benzanilide group [ArC(=O)N(R)Ar', where Ar and Ar' are phenyl or substituted phenyl groups].
Any anilide fungicide whose structure contains a furanilide group [ArC(=O)N(R)Ar', where Ar is a furanyl or substituted furanyl group and Ar' is a phenyl or substituted phenyl group].
Any anilide fungicide whose structure contains a sulfonanilide group [ArSO<small><sub>2</sub></small>N(R)Ar', where Ar and Ar' represent phenyl or substituted phenyl groups].

An amide fungicide whose structure contains a phenylsulfamide moiety [ArN(R<small><sup>1</small></sup>)SO<small><sub>2</sub></small>NR<small><sup>2</small></sup>R<small><sup>3</small></sup>, where Ar represents phenyl or substituted phenyl].
An amide fungicide whose structure contains a sulfonamide moiety.
An amide fungicide whose structure contains a valine amide moiety.

The parent member of the class of flexirubins obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of 17-(4-hydroxy-3-methylphenyl)heptadeca-2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16-octaenoic acid with one of the phenolic hydroxy groups of 2-dodecyl-5-methyl resorcinol.

Flexirubins are a unique type of pigment produced by various bacteria species characterised by a common structure comprising  non-isoprenoid ω-substituted polyene carboxylic acids esterified with 2,5-dialkylated resorcinols.
Compounds that contain a benzimidazole moiety as a key feature of their structure and which have been used as fungicides.

A mixture of polysaccharides made up from alternating <small>D</small>-galactose and 3,6-anhydro-α-<small>L</small>-galactopyranose residues joined by β-(1→3)-linkages. Some of the galactosyl units may be sulfated. Agaropectin provides the viscous properties of agar.

An amino oligosaccharide that is an undecasaccharide in which two tetrasaccharide branches, each formed from fucose, galactose, N-acetylglucosamine and mannose residues linked α(1→2), β(1→4) and β(1→2) respectively, are linked α(1→3) and α(1→6) to the mannose residue of a trisaccharide chain consisting of mannose and two N-acetylglucosamine residues all linked β(1→4) with a β-configuration of the anomeric carbon of the N-acetylglucosamine residue at the reducing end.
A cholestanoid that is 5α-cholesta-8-en-3β-ol bearing two additional methyl substituents at position 4.

An organic sodium salt that is the disodium salt of 2-amino-5-[(4-amino-3-sulfophenyl)(4-imino-3-sulfocyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-ylidene)methyl]-3-methylbenzene-1-sulfonic acid. It is used in the Van Gieson method in conjunction with picric acid to demonstrate collagen fibres red, and in Masson's trichrome to colour smooth muscle in contrast to collagen.
A 3β-sterol that is 5α-cholest-8-en-3β-ol carrying an additional hydroxymethyl substituent at position 4α.
A steroid acid anion that is the conjugate base of 3β-hydroxy-5α-cholest-8-ene-4α-carboxylic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
A lipid A oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups and protonation of the amino group of lipid II<small><sub>B</sub></small>; major species at pH 7.3.
Compounds that contain a carbamate ester moiety as a key feature of their structure and which have been used as fungicides.
Any conazole antifungal agent that has been used as a fungicide.
Any imidazole antifungal agent that has been used as a fungicide.
The iminium ion derived from acid green 5 (the disodium salt).
An L-α-amino acid residue derived from O-(N-acetyl-α-D-galactosaminyl)-L-threonine.

A naphthalenesulfonic acid that is naphthalene-1,3-disulfonic acid carrying additional hydroxy and phenyldiazenyl substituents at positions 7 and 8 respectively. The disodium salt is the biological stain 'orange G'.
An organic sodium salt having 4-hydroxy-3-[(2-methoxyphenyl)diazenyl]naphthalene-1-sulfonate as the counterion.
An organosulfonate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the sulfo group of 4-hydroxy-3-[(2-methoxyphenyl)diazenyl]naphthalene-1-sulfonic acid.
A pentacyclic triterpenoid that is olean-12-ene substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 16, an oxo group at position 23 and a carboxy group at position 28 (the 3β,16α stereoisomer).
Any triazole antifungal agent that has been used as a fungicide.
An organic heterotetracyclic compound that is 1,6-dihydrobenzo[h]imidazo[4,5-f]isoquinolin-7-one bearing additional tert-butyl and fluoro substituents at positions 2 and 9 respectively.
A polyunsaturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of juvenile hormone I carboxylic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

A naphthalenesulfonic acid that is naphthalene-1,3-disulfonic acid carrying additional hydroxy and (naphthalen-1-yl)diazenylsubstituents at positions 7 and 8 respectively. The disodium salt is the biological stain 'acid red 44'.
A methyl-branched fatty acyl-CoA(4−) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of (R)-2-hydroxy-4-methylpentanoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
A monounsaturated fatty acyl-CoA(4−) arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions of 4-methylpent-2-enoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.
An organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of 5-epi-valiolone 7-phosphate; major species at pH 7.3.
An organonitrogen compound that contains an amino group that is attached to a carbon which is itself attached to an olefinic carbon and which has been used as an antifungal drug.
A TDP-sugar having actinospectose as the sugar component.

A member of the class of isoquinolines that is (3S)-2-L-alanyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline-3-carboxylic acid in which the α-amino group of the alanyl residue has been substituted by a 1-ethoxycarbonyl-4-phenylbutan-2-yl group (the all-S isomer). A prodrug for quinaprilat (by hydrolysis of the ethyl ester to the corresponding carboxylic acid), it is used as an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACE inhibitor) used (generally as the hydrochloride salt) for the treatment of hypertension and congestive heart failure.
An N-acylglycine in which the acyl group is specified as myristoyl (tetradecanoyl).
An enamide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of (Z)-11-methyldodec-2-enoic acid with the amino group of cyclopropylamine.
A long-chain fatty acid ethyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of dodec-2-enoic acid with the hydroxy group of ethanol.
A fatty amide resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of (Z)-dodec-2-enoic acid with the nitrogen of piperidine.
A C45 carotenoid that is an intermediate in the biosynthesis of bacterioruberin, a red-coloured pigment found in several Halobacterium and Haloarcula species
An organic anionic group that is the conjugate base of 5-taurinomethyluridine 5'-phosphate residue; major species at pH 7.3.
A (2R)-2-methylacyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (2R)-2-methyltetradecanoic acid.
A hexosamine that is <small>D</small>-psicose in which the hydroxy group at position 1 is replaced by an amino group (substituted or unsubstituted).
An organosulfonate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the sulfo groups of Biebrich scarlet.

A naphthalenesulfonic acid that is 7-hydroxynaphthalene-1,3-disulfonic acid substituted at position 8 by a [4-(phenyldiazenyl)phenyl]diazenyl group. The disodium salt is the biological stain 'woodstain scarlet'.

An organic sodium salt that is the disodium salt of 2,3,4,5-tetrachloro-6-(2,4,5,7-tetrabromo-6-hydroxy-3-oxo-3H-xanthen-9-yl)benzoic acid. It is used in the hematoxylin phloxine saffron (HPS) stain, stains paneth cell granules in Lendrum's phloxine-tartrazine method, and can be used to demonstrate alcoholic hyaline.
A dicarboximide fungicide whose structure contains a phthalimide derivative.

A xanthene dye that is fluorescein bearing bromine substituents at positions 2', 4', 5' and 7' (on the xanthene ring) and iodine substituents at position 2, 3, 4, and 5 (on the phenyl ring). The dipotassium salt is the biological stain 'rose bengal'.
Any pyrimidine antifungal agent that has been used for the treatment of fungal infections in humans or animals.
A member of the class of furans in which the furan ring is substituted by a nitro group and which also has significant antibiotic properties.
A gallate ester obtained by the formal condensation of gallic acid with ethanol.
A monoglyceride in which the acyl contains a total of 14 carbon atoms and 0 double bonds.
A monoglyceride in which the acyl group contains a total of 16 carbon atoms and 1 double bond.
A monoglyceride in which the acyl groups contain a total of 18 carbons and two double bonds.
A monoglyceride in which the acyl group contains a total of 18 carbon atoms and 3 double bonds.
An o-quinone resulting from the formal oxidation of the dihydroxyphenyl moiety of 2-hydroxyestrone.
An olefinic compound that is butanal substituted by a methyl group at position 3 and a [(1Z)-prop-1-en-1-yl]oxy group at position 4 respectively.
A member of the class of cyclopentanes that is cyclopentane substituted by a 1-methylbutyl group.
An acetate ester that is propyl acetate substituted by an ethoxy group at position 3.
A butan-4-olide that is γ-butanolactone substituted by a 1-hydroxyethyl group at position 4.
derivative of glyburide (CHEBI:5441), also known as azidoglibenclamide
A member of the class of azulenes that is azulene substituted by methyl groups at positions 4, 6 and 8 respectively.
A primary alcohol that is butan-1-ol substituted by a chloro group at position 4.
An  acetylenic compound that is deca-4,6-diyne substituted by methyl groups at positions 3 and 8 and hydroxy groups at positions 3 and 8 respectively.
A tetratriacontapentaenoate that is the conjugate base of (16Z,19Z,22Z,25Z,28Z)-tetratriacontapentaenoic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

A dibenzoazepine that is 5,7-dihydro-6H-dibenzo[b,d]azepin-6-one which is substituted at the 7 pro-S position by the C-terminal carboxamide nitrogen of N2-[(2S)-2-(3,5-difluorophenyl)-2-hydroxyacetyl]-L-alaninamide. It is a potent, cell permeable and selective γ-secretase inhibitor. It has been tested as a possible treatment for Alzheimer's disease and shows promise for its potential to counteract severe hearing loss.
An amino hexasaccharide consisting of six N-formyl-α-D-perosamine residues linked sequentially (1→2), (1→3), (1→2), (1→2) and (1→2).
An organosulfonate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the sulfo groups of 1,3,4,5,7,8-hexahydroxy-9,10-dioxo-9,10-dihydroanthracene-2,6-disulfonic acid.
An octanoate ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of octanoic acid (caprylic acid) with the hydroxy group of propan-1-ol.

An organic sodium salt that is the trisodium salt of 5-[(3-carboxy-5-methyl-4-oxocyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-ylidene)(2-sulfophenyl)methyl]-2-hydroxy-3-methylbenzoic acid. It can be used for the detection of some metals in tissue.
An alicyclic ketone that is bicyclo[2.2.2]octane carrying two oxo groups located at positions 2 and 6.
A fatty acid ethyl ester resulting from the formal condensation of octanoic acid with ethanol.
A fatty acid ethyl ester of lauric acid.
An acyl-CoA(4−) that is the tetraanion of lithocholyl-CoA, arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions; major species at pH 7.3.

A monohydroxypyridine that is pyridine in which the hydrogen at position 3 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It has been detected as a thermal degradation product from the smoke of the burning leaves of Salvia divinorum, a Mexican psychoactive plant.

An amino oligosaccharide that is an undecasaccharide derivative in which two α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-β-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl tetrasaccharide chains are linked (1→3) and (1→6) to the mannose residue of a β-D-mannosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine trisaccharide.
An acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of dihydrocaffeic acid.
A polyether that is the bis(4-guanidinophenyl) ether of propane-1,3-diol. Used (as its isethionate salt) for the treatment of minor eye or eyelid infections, such as conjunctivitis and blepharitis.

An organic sodium salt that is the trisodium salt of 4,4'-{({4-[(4-sulfophenyl)imino]cyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-ylidene}methylene)bis[(4,1-phenylene)azanediyl]}di(benzene-1-sulfonic acid). A histological dye that can be used either on its own or part of a mixture (aniline blue WS) for staining collagen in Masson's trichrome and Mallory's method for connective tissue.
A hydroxy fatty acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of (R)-2-hydroxybutanoic acid.
A mixture comprising four closely related phenazine derivatives mauveine A, mauveine B, mauveine B2 and  mauveine C. A violet coloured dye.

An organic cation consisting of 1,8-dimethyl-3-(4-methylanilino)phenazine carrying additional phenyl and amino substituents at positions 5 and 7 respectively. One of four components of mauvaine, a syntheteic violet-coloured dye.

An organic cation consisting of 7-(4-methylanilino)phenazine carrying additional methyl, amino and 4-methylphenyl substituents at positions 2, 3 and 5 respectively. One of four components of mauvaine, a syntheteic violet-coloured dye.
An organosulfonate salt composed from 2-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene-1-diazonium and 5-sulfonaphthalene-1-sulfonate in a 1:1 ratio. Used for demostrating enterochromaffin in carcinoid tumours.
A fatty acid methyl ester of 10-undecenoic acid.
A fatty acid methyl ester of lauric acid.
The acetate ester of octan-1-ol.
An alkylamine that is pent-3-en-1-amine substituted by a methyl group ay position 4.
The acetate ester of nonan-1-ol.
An alkene that is hex-1-ene substituted by methyl groups at positions 4 and 5 respectively.
An amino tetrasaccharide consisting of α-D-galactose, β-D-galactose, N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine and N-acetyl-β-D-galactosamine residues connected in sequence by (1→3) linkages.
An alkadiene that is hexa-1,4-diene substituted by methyl groups at positions 2 and 3 respectively.
A carboxylic ester obtained by the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 2-hydroxypropanoic acid  with the hydroxy group of isoamylol.

A carboxylic ester obtained by formal condensation between the carboxy group of (1R,3S)-3-(2,2-dichloroethenyl)-2,2-dimethylcyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid and the hydroxy group of (4S)-4-hydroxy-3-methyl-2-(prop-2-yn-1-yl)cyclopent-2-en-1-one.
A member of the class of tetrazoles that is 1H-tetrazole substituted by amino groups at positions 1 and 5 respectively.
A fatty acid ethyl ester of 3-hexenoic acid.
A 6β-hydroxy steroid that is androst-4-ene-3,17-dione substituted by a β-hydroxy group at position 6.

An amino oligosaccharide that is a dodecasaccharide derivative consisting of a tetrasaccharide chain of N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine, β-D-mannose, N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residues, all linked sequentially (1→4), to the β-D-mannose residue of which are also linked β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-[β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→6)]-α-D-mannosyl and β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl units via (1→6) and (1→3) linkages respectively.
A fatty acid ethyl ester of 4-octenoic acid.

A carboxylic ester obtained by formal condensation of the carboxy group of (1R,3R)-3-[(1Z)-2-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoroprop-1-enyl]-2,2-dimethylcyclopropanecarboxylic acid with the hydroxy group of [(2-methyl-1,1'-biphenyl)-3-yl]methanol.
An amino disaccharide that consists of N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine having a 6-O-sulfo-β-D-galactosyl residue attached at position 3.
A 3-hydroxy steroid that is 17β-estradiol substituted by an α-hydroxy group at position 15.

An amino oligosaccharide that is an undecaasaccharide derivative in which two α-L-fucosyl-(1→2)-[N-acetyl-β-D-galactosaminyl-(1→3)]-β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl chains are linked (1→3) and (1→6) to D-galactose.
A 3-hydroxy steroid that is 17β-estradiol substituted by a β-hydroxy group at position 16.

A branched amino oligosaccharide comprising a linear trisaccharide of β-D-mannose and two N-acetyl-β-D-glucosamine residues all linked in sequence (1→4), to the mannosyl residue of which is (1→4)-linked an Nacetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl residue, together with two N-acetyl-α-neuraminyl-(2→3)-β-D-galactosyl-(1→4)-N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminyl-(1→2)-α-D-mannosyl tetrasaccharide units linked (1→3) and (1→6).
A 3-hydroxy steroid that is estrone substituted by a β-hydroxy group at position 16.

Any organooxygen compound whose structure is related to compactin (mevastatin) and which may be used as an anticholesteremic drug due its EC 1.1.1.34/EC 1.1.1.88 (hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA reductase) inhibitory properties.
A statin that is derived from a naturally occurring statin by partial chemical synthesis.
An organic cation that is phenothiazin-5-ium substituted by amino and dimethylamino groups at positions 3 and 7 respectively. The chloride salt is the histological dye 'azure A'.

A carboxylic ester resulting from the formal condensation between the carboxylic acid group of mycophenolic acid and the hydroxy group of 2-(morpholin-4-yl)ethanol. In the liver, it is metabolised to mycophenolic acid, an immunosuppressant for which it is a prodrug. It is widely used to prevent tissue rejection following organ transplants as well as for the treatment of certain autoimmune diseases.
An organic cation that is phenothiazin-5-ium substituted by amino and methylamino groups at positions 3 and 7 respectively. The chloride salt is the histological dye 'azure C'.
Any fatty acid ester in which the carboxylic acid component is lauric acid.
A four-component mixture of chemically related dyes comprising pararosanilin, rosanilin, magenta II and new fuchsin in varying amounts
An iminium ion obtained by protonation of the imino group of new fuchsin free base.
A steroid acid anion that is the conjugate base of (25R)-3β-hydroxycholest-5-en-7-one-26-oic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
The fatty acid ethyl ester of  3-hydroxybutyric acid.
A member of the class of benzenes that is benzene substituted by a [(methanesulfonyl)methanesulfonyl]methyl group.
An 2,3-trans-enoyl CoA(4−) obtained by deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of (2E,5Z)-tetradecadienoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.

A member of the class of 1-benzothiophenes that is 1-benzothiophene in which the hydrogens at positions 2, 3, and 6 have been replaced by p-hydroxyphenyl, p-[2-(piperidin-1-yl)ethoxy]benzoyl, and hydroxy groups, respectively.
A monounsaturated fatty acid anion that is the conjugate base of (2E)-hexenoic acid.
An organic cation resulting from the protonation of the amino group of (R)-prasugrel.
A bile acid anion that is the conjugate base of 7α-hydroxy-3-oxo-5β-cholan-24-oic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.
